sections.subtitle: Match context
sections.text: Sunderland host Manchester United at the Stadium of Light. United sit 3rd (64 points) and Sunderland are 12th (47). Sofascore’s model favours an away win (home 31%, draw 25%, away 44%) and gives a 56% chance of both teams to score.

sections.subtitle: Current form
sections.text: Sunderland’s last 5: 2 wins, 1 draw, 2 losses, including a 0-5 setback against Nottingham Forest and a 1-1 at Wolverhampton. United arrive on a 3‑match winning run (Chelsea 0-1, Brentford 2-1, Liverpool 3-2) with the better recent expected goals profile.

sections.subtitle: Head-to-head
sections.text: United won the last 2 meetings without conceding (2-0 in 2025, 3-0 in 2017). Trends point to the visitors starting fast: ‘first to score’ in 6/7, and more than 2.5 goals in 4/5 head-to-heads. Sunderland are without a clean sheet in the last 7 against United.

sections.subtitle: Season stats and matchup
sections.text: Sunderland have struggled in attack (37 goals, 17th; 58 big chances, 17th; 34% conversion) and play with lower possession (44%) and accuracy (79%), while facing shot volume (opponents’ shots 14.6 per match) but keeping games competitive (46 conceded, 7th fewest). United have scored 63 and conceded 48, and finish strongly (29% of goals in 76–90). Aerially, Harry Maguire’s duel win rate (79%) and Bruno Fernandes’ chance creation (19 assists, league‑leading key passes) are notable edges.

sections.subtitle: Key players
sections.text: For Sunderland, Enzo Le Fée (5 assists) and Brian Brobbey (6 goals) carry threat, with Nordi Mukiele adding 3 goals and 4 assists from defence. For United, Bruno Fernandes is in form (last 5: 1 goal, 3 assists), and Amad Diallo has troubled Sunderland before (2 goals across recent meetings).

sections.subtitle: Referee, cards and corners
sections.text: Referee Stuart Attwell averages 3.5 yellows per match. Sunderland average 2.2 yellows and both teams show recent ‘over 4.5 cards’ tendencies. Corners trend lower here (Sunderland 3.5 per match; ‘under 10.5 corners’ in 5/6 Sunderland home and 4/5 head-to-heads).

sections.subtitle: Match prediction
sections.text: United’s recent momentum and superior chance creation make them slight favourites, in line with the model. Sunderland’s late resilience keeps them competitive, but United’s stronger finish and set‑piece and aerial advantages tilt the balance. ‘Both teams to score’ is a plausible outcome.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match context and first-half summary
halftimeSections.text: Goalless at the break at the Stadium of Light, with Sunderland the stronger side on the balance of play. They lead on shots on target (3-0), big chances (1-0) and expected goals (0.97-0.30). Territory has favoured the hosts as well (final third entries 37-18; penalty area entries 21-13). Sunderland have also been more robust in duels (55% won) and in the air (63%), while winning possession 5 times in the final third compared with Manchester United’s 1.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Tactical patterns and spaces
halftimeSections.text: Sunderland’s midfield have controlled central zones and circulated the ball efficiently to sustain pressure, with quick support around the box and regular entries into the area. Their ability to win second balls has kept United pinned for long spells. Manchester United’s build-up has been slow under pressure, with limited runners beyond the ball. Most of their threat has come in moments when they have advanced their full-backs and found pockets for the forwards to receive, but these have been isolated.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Key performers
halftimeSections.text: For Sunderland, Enzo Le Fée has been the main creator (3 key passes, 1 big chance created), Granit Xhaka has anchored midfield well (2 tackles won, 2 interceptions), and Noah Sadiki produced the clearest opening (0.43 xG, 1 big chance missed). Reinildo has dealt with danger in wide areas (4 clearances), while Brian Brobbey has linked play and tested the goalkeeper (2 key passes, 1 shot on target). For Manchester United, Senne Lammens has been their standout, keeping them level, with Kobbie Mainoo the most likely from midfield in advanced positions. Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martínez have handled several crosses but have lacked protection in front at times.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Attack momentum
halftimeSections.text: Sunderland controlled the early phase with sustained pressure and multiple attacking spells. Manchester United responded around the half-hour mark with a brief period of initiative. The hosts then reasserted themselves before United finished the half with a short attacking spell heading into the interval. Overall momentum slightly favours Sunderland.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Expected goals and chance quality
halftimeSections.text: Sunderland’s 0.97 expected goals from 3 shots on target reflects one high-value opening and consistent entries into dangerous areas. Manchester United’s 0.30 expected goals came from lower-quality situations and did not translate into shots on target. With the home side repeatedly accessing the box and winning more duels, the platform for a second-half breakthrough is present, although United remain a threat if they can speed up their attacks and commit more runners.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Referee, cards and corners
halftimeSections.text: No cards are listed at half-time. Corners are level at 4-4, reflecting Sunderland’s sustained pressure and United’s late response. Expect a slight rise in intensity after the restart, likely 1-3 cards overall in the second half. Given territorial trends, Sunderland can edge the corner count by full-time, with approximately 4-6 more corners to come.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Second-half outlook
halftimeSections.text: If Sunderland maintain their press and continue to find quick combinations around the box, they are well placed to strike first. Manchester United need more direct running and quicker release into the front line to shift the dynamic. The next goal probability leans towards Sunderland, with Brian Brobbey the most likely scorer from their current patterns of play. A narrow home win is the likeliest outcome if the match continues on similar terms.
